content: There is no data/conjectures.json in the repo. Should there be?
no, it should be either generated on the fly (with the extract_names script) or downloaded from the existing website, adapt instructions if needed
I would guess this is created or restored from a cache in CI?
running extract_names should be fast, the slow part is the lake build, which we run in the ci for other reasons
Ok I will edit the README.md in my PR then, if that is fine.
I am a bit confused by the wording, the Github CI doesnt commit the conjectures.json or does it? Should data/conjectures.json then belong to the gitignore?
yes, adding to .gitignore would be a good idea!
Ok, I will change the wording from committing to adding in the README.md then.
General Question about the Website, does it really make sense to include test / API statements? I think those are fairly uninteresting from a benchmark / user perspective.

Yeah, perhaps we could add a convenient way to filter them out? Like deselection by default?
Right now the user interface is a bit strange (in the same way many other filtering mechanism on websites work): default is not selecting anything, which means nothing is filtered. As soon as you select something it deselects everything else.
not sure how one could make the ui better. I do think there is some benefit to see the test and API statements

regarding counting: I think we should add counter for files as well, so like "18 statements in 4 files" or something like that to avoid inflating our number and listing more problems that items in a specific problem list (see also #Formal conjectures > New Website @ 💬 )

I currently also have a PR in draft for changing the Total Problem count to be just Solved + Open + Formally Solved. I have also thought about the best way of counting and / or showing the "right" number of problems.

I have also thought of just adding a small note, because the other options feel so overengineer like. If we add a X statements in Y files, then shouldn't we also use the files as our problem count instead of statements? In some cases file is more canonical, in some cases statement. Like in the RH file, we have 3 statements, which would be considered 3 problems.

I agree that we should try to count problems differently. Perhaps the most flexible solution here is to implement an attribute main_problem (we can have several per file if they correspond to genuinely different mathematical questions). Each such problem would the increment the count by 1.
For example, in the Millenium Problems dir, only the actual millenium problems should have that attribute (and if we have several equivalent formalisations, we pick one)
Funny, I also had this idea like 10 minutes ago :D.
I’ll open a PR to implement this sometime soon
